methodological_rigor.justification: This is a large-scale biobank epidemiologic study in 419,154 UK Biobank participants with 13.8-year median follow-up (463 CLL cases) plus an independent replication in 40,930 All of Us participants (87 CLL cases) using a case-cohort design with appropriate weighting. Heteroplasmy is measured via WGS using the MitoHPC/Mutect2 pipeline with pre-specified QC filters (depth, base/mapping quality, strand bias, haplogroup/NUMT contamination, homopolymer exclusion). A modified mitochondrial local constraint (mMLC) score is developed and aggregated (mMSS) to capture deleterious variant burden. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models are adjusted for age (restricted cubic spline, 4 df), sex, smoking, and prior cancer; robustness analyses include VAF thresholds (3%, 5%, 10%), adjustment for mtDNA copy number and blood counts, and case-cohort weighting. Limitations are in nature inherent to observational epidemiology (unmeasured confounders, reliance on ICD codes) but the design is exemplary for biobank-scale risk-factor studies.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Prospective cohort analysis of UKB with independent replication in AoU case-cohort; Oxford LoE 2b. Clinical relevance is high: identifies mitochondrial heteroplasmy (especially functionally deleterious variants via mMSS) as an independent CLL risk biomarker that captures individuals missed by L-CHIP-based assessment (HR 1.5 for any heteroplasmy, HR 4.0 for mMSS after adjustment). This could inform CLL risk stratification, surveillance, and future preventive trials.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE applies for this prospective observational biomarker study. The methods report UKB REC and AoU IRB approvals and written informed consent; inclusion/exclusion criteria with explicit counts (excluded n=14,267 missing L-CHIP, n=201 prior CLL, n=682 lymphocytosis); variable definitions (VAF thresholds, lymphocytosis, anemia); pipeline version (MitoHPC 20230418); covariates and statistical models; and sensitivity analyses. CLL case ascertainment via UKB cancer registry ICD-9/10 codes through December 22, 2022 is explicit. AoU case-cohort design with weights is appropriately described. Source Data files are referenced throughout. A Nature Portfolio Reporting Summary is linked.

novelty_literature.justification: Prior work by the authors linked heteroplasmy to hematologic malignancies broadly (ref 14) and to myeloid neoplasms (ref 15); this study is the first to establish heteroplasmy - and specifically deleterious variants via mMSS - as an independent CLL risk factor beyond L-CHIP, with replication in AoU. Complex-specific effects (complex IV stronger for MN than CLL) add mechanistic nuance. The mMLC/mMSS scoring framework is a study-specific refinement. While the general concept of heteroplasmy-malignancy association is established, the CLL-specific, L-CHIP-independent finding with replication is novel.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is exceptionally well organized with precise effect sizes, 95% CIs, P-values in text, and clear tables with covariate definitions. Supplementary tables and figures are systematically cited. Methods are comprehensive and reproducible. Tables 1 and 2 provide crisp cohort characterization by L-CHIP/M-CHIP status. Language is clean and focused.

key_strengths: Very large prospective UKB cohort (419,154 participants; 13.8-year median follow-up; 463 CLL cases) with independent AoU case-cohort replication (87 CLL cases) using appropriate weighting
Novel mMLC/mMSS framework quantifying deleterious heteroplasmy burden; HR 4.0 (95% CI 2.7-5.9) for mMSS independent of heteroplasmy count, suggesting a possible causal role
Rigorous multivariable Cox modeling with restricted cubic splines, sensitivity analyses across VAF thresholds (3%/5%/10%), and adjustment for mtDNA-CN and blood counts
Clear clinical translation: identifies L-CHIP-negative individuals at elevated CLL risk, with direct implications for future risk stratification
key_concerns: AoU follow-up is short (median 3.9 years) with few events (87 CLL cases), limiting long-term effect estimation
ICD-code-based CLL ascertainment can miss indolent cases not requiring registration
Self-reported White predominance in UKB (94.4%) limits generalizability to diverse populations
P-values for cohort-characteristic comparisons are reported without multiple-testing correction, though this is transparent and standard for descriptive tables
chief_reviewer.rationale: A rigorously designed, transparently reported, large-scale biobank study with independent replication that establishes a novel independent CLL risk biomarker; top-tier plausible (e.g., Nature Medicine) with minor revisions for confounding sensitivity and generalizability.
